fixes.explanation: That's right, baker. The LORD swore an oath to David, and the promise is, “One of your descendants I will place on your throne.” (Psalm 132:11). Notice it's called a promise He will not revoke. That's about as solid as a promise gets.
No visitors in this oath, baker. David's list is his house, his bed, and sleep for his eyes and eyelids (Psalm 132:3-4). Nobody on that list is a guest. The song never mentions visitors at all.

Yes, baker. The group says, “Let us go to His dwelling place; let us worship at His footstool.” They're not just saying it to the air. They're inviting each other, which I love, because worship is better with company. Even a stamper who works alone like me ends up with a crowd around the cookie box eventually.

The vow was David's, baker, back in verses 2 through 5. This group is doing something different. They say, “Let us go to His dwelling place; let us worship at His footstool.” The invitation is to worship, not to make a vow.

Testing isn't what the song asks about, baker. The request is, “For the sake of Your servant David, do not reject Your anointed one.” (Psalm 132:10). The word is reject. Nothing in that line is about tests.

Yes, baker. The song asked, “May Your priests be clothed with righteousness…” (Psalm 132:9), and the LORD says, “I will clothe her priests with salvation…” (Psalm 132:16). The first is a request for righteousness, and the LORD's own words speak of salvation. Both times it's about the priests.

It's actually True, friend. The LORD says, “I will clothe her priests with salvation…” (Psalm 132:16). Earlier the song asked for righteousness (Psalm 132:9), and here the LORD speaks of salvation. Both times it's about the priests.
